messages:
max: Heads up — I'm starting a small schema rename: console.metrics.route_id -> console.metrics.route_key. Goal: make routing metadata consistent with route catalog. Need safe-read protocol for dashboards, quota lookups, and analytics backfills.

marta: What's the timeline? any backfill needed?

max: short plan: 1) dual-write at ingest layer for 2 weeks, 2) add read adapter that prefers route_key but falls back to route_id, 3) run backfill for hot partitions and verify dashboards, 4) cutover reads.

shiv: dual-write at ingest sounds good. For read adapter, can we do a DB view to unify column names so dashboards don't change? Views are nice but might blow up on p99 queries unless we materialize. :thinking_face:

leo: +1 on view for dev-console queries. For high QPS paths (quotas), we should add a small read-time coalesce in the query to avoid full-table scans. Example: SELECT COALESCE(route_key, route_id) AS route_key, ... FROM console.metrics WHERE ...

kai: telemetry ingestion will produce both fields in the envelope? We can extend the ingest contract to emit both keys. That will let dedicated console consumers switch incrementally.

max: yes, ingest will emit both for dual-write. We need to ensure the compact index on route id doesn't double index. Proposal: write route_key as a new indexed column and keep route_id index until backfill completes, then drop route_id index.

marta: any impact on quota routing? dashboards that group by route_id will need to switch grouping. We should add a compatibility mapper in the metrics pipeline to translate old ids to new keys for historic data.

shiv: mapper in pipeline is OK but expensive. I prefer backfilling hot shards first. We can do a shadow transformation: run an analytics job that writes route_key into a shadow table for top 1k routes, validate, then expand.

leo: for safety, add a feature-flagged read adapter at the service layer. Pseudocode: 

```sql
-- read adapter example
SELECT *, COALESCE(metrics.route_key, metrics.route_id) AS route_key_normalized
FROM console.metrics WHERE route_key_normalized = $ROUTE
```

and at service layer: if feature_flag(backfill_complete) then prefer route_key index, else use normalized column with fallback.

kai: infra note: if we do dual-write, we must ensure idempotency in ingest (same seq id) to avoid duplicates. Also watch storage growth during the window.

infra-bot: Deployment checklist created: https://internal/tasks/RED-3241 - includes dual-write rollout, canary plan, and index drop steps.

max: recommended rollout: canary on one tenant (tenant_42) for 24h, monitor p95/p99 of quota lookups, dashboard query latencies, and errors. Backfill hot shards day 1. If stable, expand to 10% of traffic then full.

marta: metrics to track: query p99, backfill throughput, storage delta, dashboard diff (compare counts by route pre/post). Add regression alert on dashboard diffs > 0.5%.

shiv: small suggestion on SQL backfill snippet: 

```sql
-- backfill hot shard example
INSERT INTO console.metrics (ts, route_key, ...)
SELECT ts, COALESCE(route_key, route_id) AS route_key, ... FROM console.metrics_old WHERE route_id IN (SELECT route_id FROM hot_routes_limit)
```

leo: also add a read-only API layer change: accept route_key param but accept route_id for legacy callers; server normalizes both into internal route_key for downstream. That lets API consumers migrate at their own pace.

max: decision summary: dual-write at ingest + idempotent writes; read adapter/coalesce in service + DB view for non-critical queries; targeted backfill for hot shards; canary tenant then ramp; drop old route_id index after backfill and final verification.

kai: I'll schedule the ingest contract update and add schema migration runbook steps.

marta: ok, please put the action items in the runbook and tag infra for index drop. I'll coordinate dashboard owners for validation. :thumbsup:

max: thanks — I'll start the dual-write PR and link it here.
